1→---
     2→name: arch-review-guide
     3→description: Use this skill when reviewing or working on project architecture. Provides quick reference for architecture violation detection, dependency direction rules, and structural health assessment across Kotlin, Python, and TypeScript/JavaScript.
     4→---
     5→
     6→# Architecture Review Quick Reference
     7→
     8→This skill provides a condensed checklist for identifying architecture violations during code review or development.
     9→
    10→## When to Activate
    11→
    12→- Reviewing code that changes project structure or adds new modules
    13→- Working with dependency injection, layer boundaries, or module dependencies
    14→- Creating new packages, directories, or modules
    15→- Refactoring architecture (extracting services, separating layers)
    16→- Reviewing import statements for dependency direction compliance
    17→- Evaluating DTO/Entity separation or data flow patterns
    18→- Assessing microservice communication patterns
    19→
    20→## Core Principles
    21→
    22→### 1. Dependencies Flow Inward
    23→Outer layers depend on inner layers, never the reverse. Domain/core has zero outward dependencies.
    24→
    25→```
    26→[Controller/API] --> [Service/UseCase] --> [Domain/Entity] --> [nothing]
    27→     ^                     ^                    ^
    28→     |                     |                    |
    29→[Infrastructure]    [Infrastructure]      [NEVER depends on outer]
    30→```
    31→
    32→### 2. Detect, Don't Prescribe
    33→Report the detected architecture style. Don't force hexagonal on a simple CRUD app. Match analysis to project maturity.
    34→
    35→### 3. Context Matters
    36→Read surrounding code before flagging. A pattern that looks bad in isolation may be an intentional trade-off.
    37→
    38→## 6-Step Analysis Workflow
    39→
    40→| Step | Name | What to Check |
    41→|------|------|--------------|
    42→| 1 | Macro Structure Discovery | Build configs, module composition, project type |
    43→| 2 | Dependency Direction Tracking | Import analysis, layer violation detection |
    44→| 3 | Package Structure & Naming | Naming conventions, package-by-layer vs feature |
    45→| 4 | Data Modeling Strategy | DTO/Entity separation, CQRS patterns |
    46→| 5 | MSA / Distributed System | Message brokers, service discovery, resilience |
    47→| 6 | Developer Intent & Health | Git history, test coverage, exception handling |
    48→
    49→## Quick Reference by Violation Type
    50→
    51→### Critical Violations
    52→| ID | Violation | Fix | Detection |
    53→|----|-----------|-----|-----------|
    54→| V-C1 | Domain depends on infrastructure | Pure domain model + separate persistence entity | `import javax.persistence` in `domain/**` |
    55→| V-C2 | Circular module dependencies | Shared events/interfaces, event-driven communication | Bidirectional imports between modules |
    56→| V-C3 | UseCase depends on concrete adapter | Depend on port interfaces only | `import adapter.*` in `usecase/**` |
    57→
    58→### High Violations
    59→| ID | Violation | Fix | Detection |
    60→|----|-----------|-----|-----------|
    61→| V-H1 | Layer skipping (Controller -> Repository) | Controller -> Service -> Repository | `Repository` in `controller/**` |
    62→| V-H2 | Entity exposed to API | Map to DTO before responding | `ResponseEntity<*Entity>` in controllers |
    63→| V-H3 | Business logic in controller | Move to service layer | `calculate/validate/process` in controllers |
    64→| V-H4 | Hard-coded dependencies (no DI) | Constructor injection | `= new *Repository()` or `= *Service()` |
    65→
    66→### Medium Violations
    67→| ID | Violation | Fix | Detection |
    68→|----|-----------|-----|-----------|
    69→| V-M1 | Inconsistent naming convention | Follow language conventions (PEP8, Kotlin style) | `class [a-z]`, `def camelCase` |
    70→| V-M2 | Package structure inconsistency | Choose one: package-by-layer OR package-by-feature | Mixed `controllers/` + `order/` directories |
    71→| V-M3 | God class / God module | Extract responsibilities, apply SRP | Files > 500 lines, > 15 imports |
    72→
    73→### Low Violations
    74→| ID | Violation | Fix | Detection |
    75→|----|-----------|-----|-----------|
    76→| V-L1 | Missing architecture tests | Add ArchUnit / dependency-cruiser | No `@ArchTest` or `dependency-cruiser` |
    77→| V-L2 | Missing API documentation | Add springdoc / swagger | No `openapi` in build config |
    78→| V-L3 | No error handling strategy | Add global exception handler | No `@ControllerAdvice` / `ExceptionFilter` |
    79→
    80→## Top 5 Most Common Architecture Violations
    81→
    82→### 1. Domain Depends on Infrastructure (V-C1)
    83→```kotlin
    84→// BAD: domain/model/Order.kt
    85→import javax.persistence.Entity  // Infrastructure leak!
    86→
    87→// GOOD: Pure domain model + infrastructure/persistence/OrderEntity.kt
    88→data class Order(val id: OrderId, val customerId: CustomerId, val totalAmount: Money)
    89→```
    90→
    91→### 2. Controller Skipping Service Layer (V-H1)
    92→```kotlin
    93→// BAD
    94→@RestController
    95→class OrderController(private val orderRepository: OrderRepository) { ... }
    96→
    97→// GOOD
    98→@RestController
    99→class OrderController(private val orderService: OrderService) { ... }
   100→```
   101→
   102→### 3. Entity Exposed to API (V-H2)
   103→```python
   104→# BAD
   105→@router.get("/users/{id}")
   106→async def get_user(id: int, db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
   107→    return db.query(UserModel).get(id)  # Leaks all fields
   108→
   109→# GOOD
   110→@router.get("/users/{id}", response_model=UserResponse)
   111→async def get_user(id: int, service: UserService = Depends()):
   112→    return service.find_by_id(id)
   113→```
   114→
   115→### 4. Hard-coded Dependencies (V-H4)
   116→```typescript
   117→// BAD
   118→export class OrderService {
   119→    private repo = new PostgresOrderRepo() // Tight coupling!
   120→}
   121→
   122→// GOOD
   123→@Injectable()
   124→export class OrderService {
   125→    constructor(private readonly repo: OrderRepository) {}
   126→}
   127→```
   128→
   129→### 5. Business Logic in Controller (V-H3)
   130→```kotlin
   131→// BAD: Controller calculates, validates, notifies
   132→@PostMapping("/orders")
   133→fun createOrder(@RequestBody req: CreateOrderRequest): ResponseEntity<OrderDto> {
   134→    val total = req.items.sumOf { it.price * it.quantity }
   135→    if (total > 10000) notificationService.notifyAdmin("Large order")
   136→    // ...
   137→}
   138→
   139→// GOOD: Delegate to service
   140→@PostMapping("/orders")
   141→fun createOrder(@RequestBody req: CreateOrderRequest): ResponseEntity<OrderDto> {
   142→    return ResponseEntity.status(HttpStatus.CREATED).body(orderService.create(req))
   143→}
   144→```
   145→
   146→## Architecture Identification Matrix
   147→
   148→| Signal | Architecture Type |
   149→|--------|-------------------|
   150→| `controller/`, `service/`, `repository/` dirs | Layered |
   151→| `@Controller`, `@Service`, `@Repository` | Layered |
   152→| `port/`, `adapter/`, `usecase/` dirs | Hexagonal/Clean |
   153→| `domain/` with no outward imports | Hexagonal/Clean |
   154→| `views.py`, `models.py`, `urls.py` | Django MVT |
   155→| `modules/` with `*.module.ts` | NestJS Modular |
   156→
   157→## DTO Separation Maturity
   158→
   159→| Level | Description | Quality |
   160→|-------|-------------|---------|
   161→| 0 | Entity used everywhere | Poor |
   162→| 1 | DTO exists but mixed with Entity | Fair |
   163→| 2 | DTO per layer (Request/Response/Domain) | Good |
   164→| 3 | CQRS (Command/Query separation) | Excellent |
   165→
   166→## MSA Maturity Levels
   167→
   168→| Level | Description |
   169→|-------|-------------|
   170→| 0 | Monolith - Single deployable unit |
   171→| 1 | Modular Monolith - Logically separated modules |
   172→| 2 | SOA - REST between services, possibly shared DB |
   173→| 3 | MSA - Independent DBs, message brokers, service discovery |
   174→| 4 | Event-Driven - Kafka/RabbitMQ primary, CQRS, Event Sourcing |
   175→
   176→## Architecture Health Score
   177→
   178→```
   179→Base: 100 points
   180→
   181→Deductions:
   182→  Critical violation: -15 each
   183→  High violation:     -8 each
   184→  Medium violation:   -3 each
   185→  Low violation:      -1 each
   186→
   187→Bonuses:
   188→  Architecture tests (ArchUnit):  +5
   189→  API documentation:              +3
   190→  Global exception handler:       +2
   191→  Consistent naming:              +3
   192→  DTO separation Level 2+:        +2
   193→
   194→Rating:
   195→  90-100: Excellent | 75-89: Good | 60-74: Fair | 40-59: Poor | 0-39: Critical
   196→```
   197→
   198→## Severity Guide
   199→
   200→| Severity | When to Flag |
   201→|----------|-------------|
   202→| **Critical** | Core architecture principle broken (dependency direction reversed, circular deps) |
   203→| **High** | Layer boundaries crossed, entity leaked to API, business logic misplaced |
   204→| **Medium** | Naming inconsistency, package structure mixing, SRP violation |
   205→| **Low** | Missing best practice (architecture tests, API docs, error handler) |
   206→
   207→## Detailed Guide
   208→
   209→For detailed analysis methodology, Bad/Good code examples per violation, and detection patterns, refer to the guide below:
   210→
   211→- **[Architecture Review Guide](./guide/arch-review-guide.md)** - Full methodology including 6-step analysis workflow, Violation Checklist (V-C1~V-L3), and Health Score calculation
   212→
   213→This skill (SKILL.md) serves as a quick reference. For in-depth analysis, use the guide's detection patterns and code examples.
   214→
   215→## Integration with Other Tools
   216→
   217→- Use `/arch-review [target]` command for structured analysis with full report
   218→- Use `/analyze --focus architecture` for broader multi-domain assessment
   219→- The `arch-reviewer` agent contains the complete methodology with all code examples
   220→- Use `/perf-review` for complementary performance-focused analysis
   221→- This skill provides quick reference during regular development
   222→
   223→---
   224→
   225→**Remember**: Architecture matters most at scale. For small CRUD apps, pragmatism beats purity. Always consider project maturity and team size when evaluating violations. Detect the intended architecture, validate conformance, and provide actionable feedback.

    83→
    84→**Tier 1: `PROJECT_ROOT/CLAUDE.md`** (always loaded, 30-50 lines)
    85→- Module/package list (names only)
    86→- Entry points, Generated files (DO NOT MODIFY)
    87→- "See .claude/rules/ for tech-specific guides"
    88→
    89→**Tier 2: `PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/rules/*.md`** (auto-loaded on path match)
    90→- Each file has frontmatter with `paths:` for auto-loading:
    91→  ```yaml
    92→  ---
    93→  description: "Kafka consumer/producer conventions"
    94→  paths: ["**/inbound-consumer/**", "**/outbound-event/**"]
    95→  ---
    96→  ```
    97→- Contains: tech-specific inverted index + conventions + pitfalls
    98→
    99→**Tier 3: `PROJECT_ROOT/{module}/CLAUDE.md`** (loaded when working in that module)
   100→- Optional, for complex modules only
   101→
   102→**Why 3-Tier?**
   103→- Root CLAUDE.md stays under 50 lines (always in context, never wasted)
   104→- Tech-specific rules load ONLY when the agent works in matching paths
   105→- Total indexed knowledge can be 10x larger without context overhead
   106→
   107→## Optimal Granularity
   108→
   109→```
   110→Safe to index          |  Do NOT index
   111→-----------------------|-----------------
   112→Module structure       |  Business class filenames
   113→Package paths          |  Test filenames
   114→Config filenames (few) |  DTO/VO class names
   115→Port/Interface names   |  Implementation file names (many)
   116→```
   117→
   118→**Module + Package level** is optimal. Agent can `ls` the package to find specific files.
   119→
   120→## Effectiveness by Language
   121→
   122→| Ecosystem | Tool Call Reduction | ROI | Killer Feature |
   123→|-----------|-------------------|-----|----------------|
   124→| Rust (Cargo workspace) | ~68% | 5-12x | Trait->Impl mapping, feature flags |
   125→| Polyglot monorepo | ~67% | 8-14x | Cross-service domain mapping |
   126→| Turborepo/Nx | ~63% | 8-14x | Cross-app impact analysis |
   127→| Python uv monorepo | ~62% | 5-12x | Name disambiguation (models/schemas) |
   128→| Go (standard layout) | ~60% | 5-10x | Interface->Impl mapping |
   129→| Next.js App Router | ~58% | 6-12x | 3-way split (app/lib/components) |
   130→| Spring Hexagonal | ~42% | 3-8x | Layer mapping (port/adapter) |
   131→
   132→## How to Use Templates
   133→
   134→Templates in `templates/` provide ready-to-use 3-Tier output for each stack.
   135→
   136→Each template contains two parts:
   137→- **Part 1: Root CLAUDE.md** -- Copy to your project's root CLAUDE.md
   138→- **Part 2: .claude/rules/ Files** -- Create each file in your `.claude/rules/` directory
   139→
   140→```
   141→templates/spring-hexagonal.md     -- Kotlin/Java multi-module
   142→templates/python-uv-monorepo.md   -- Python uv workspace
   143→templates/turborepo.md            -- TypeScript Turborepo/Nx/pnpm
   144→templates/go-standard.md          -- Go standard layout
   145→templates/rust-workspace.md       -- Rust Cargo workspace
   146→```
   147→
   148→See `references/` for detailed per-language guides:
   149→
   150→```
   151→references/lang-kotlin-java.md       -- Spring Hexagonal deep guide
   152→references/lang-python.md            -- FastAPI/Django/Celery patterns
   153→references/lang-typescript.md        -- Next.js/NestJS/Turborepo patterns
   154→references/lang-go.md                -- Go standard layout + DDD
   155→references/lang-rust.md              -- Cargo workspace + trait system
   156→references/lang-polyglot.md          -- Multi-language monorepo
   157→references/maintenance-automation.md -- Auto-generation scripts, CI checks
   158→```
   159→
   160→## Key Principles
   161→
   162→1. **Root CLAUDE.md**: 30-50 lines max (module names + entry points + generated files)
   163→2. **.claude/rules/**: One file per technology, with `paths:` frontmatter for auto-loading
   164→3. **Module + Package** granularity (not individual files)
   165→4. **Technology-grouped** format (not layer-grouped)
   166→5. **Auto-generate paths, manually curate descriptions**
   167→6. **Validate in CI** (check paths still exist)

    51→## 2. 컬렉션 설정 (`.outline-context.json`)
    52→
    53→프로젝트 루트에 배치하는 최소 설정 파일. 문서를 관리할 Outline 컬렉션 1개를 지정합니다.
    54→
    55→### 설정 파일 구조
    56→
    57→```json
    58→{
    59→  "collection_id": "uuid-of-collection",
    60→  "language": "ko",
    61→  "sensitive_patterns": ["password", "secret", "api_key", "token", "credential", "private_key", "db_password", "connection_string", "aws_access_key"]
    62→}
    63→```
    64→
    65→### 설정 파일 초기화
    66→
    67→파일이 존재하지 않을 때:
    68→1. `mcp__outline__list_collections` 호출 → 컬렉션 목록 조회
    69→2. 사용자에게 문서를 관리할 컬렉션 1개 선택 요청
    70→3. 선택된 컬렉션의 `id`로 `.outline-context.json` 자동 생성
    71→4. Git 커밋하여 팀 공유 (UUID만 포함, 보안 위험 없음)
    72→
    73→### 컬렉션 동작 방식
    74→
    75→- 모든 문서가 설정된 단일 컬렉션에 생성/업데이트됨
    76→- 문서 카테고리(api/architecture/policy/infrastructure/general)는 문서 제목 접두어로 구분
    77→  - 예: `[API] 결제 엔드포인트`, `[Architecture] 인증 모듈 구조`
    78→

    81→## 3. Behavioral Flow
    82→
    83→### Phase 1: Context Loading
    84→
    85→```
    86→1. 프로젝트 루트에서 `.outline-context.json` 파일 탐색
    87→2. 파일 존재 → JSON 파싱 → collection_id, language, sensitive_patterns 추출
    88→   파일 미존재 → 초기 설정 워크플로우 실행:
    89→     a) mcp__outline__list_collections 호출 → 컬렉션 목록 조회
    90→     b) 사용자에게 컬렉션 목록 표시 → 1개 선택 요청
    91→     c) 선택된 컬렉션 ID로 `.outline-context.json` 자동 생성
    92→     d) 생성 완료 알림
    93→3. collection_id 유효성 검증 (빈 문자열 체크)
    94→4. 검증 실패 시 → 사용자에게 알림, 재설정 안내
    95→```
    96→
    97→### Phase 2: Change Analysis
    98→
    99→```
   100→1. `git diff --name-only` → 변경 파일 목록 수집
   101→2. `git diff --stat` → 변경 통계 (파일 수, 추가/삭제 라인)
   102→3. `git log --oneline -10` → 최근 커밋 이력 수집
   103→4. MR 컨텍스트 활용 (post-merge 스킬에서 위임 호출 시):
   104→   - MR 제목/설명 → 문서 요약의 시드 데이터로 활용
   105→   - MR 라벨 → 카테고리 힌트 (api, infrastructure 등 → Phase 3 가중치 부여)
   106→   - 타겟 브랜치 → 문서화 우선순위 (main/master → 높음, develop → 보통)
   107→5. 문서화 필요 여부 판단:
   108→   - 변경 파일이 없으면 → "변경사항이 없습니다" 알림 후 종료
   109→   - 변경 파일이 설정/문서 파일만이면 → 문서화 선택적 제안
   110→   - 코드 변경이 있으면 → 문서화 진행
   111→6. 변경 파일 목록과 커밋 메시지를 Phase 3에 전달
   112→```
   113→
   114→### Phase 3: Document Type Detection
   115→
   116→파일 경로 패턴과 커밋 메시지 키워드를 분석하여 문서 카테고리를 자동 분류합니다.
   117→
   118→**파일 경로 기반 분류 (1차):**
   119→
   120→| 파일 경로 패턴 | 카테고리 | 가중치 |
   121→|---------------|---------|--------|
   122→| `controller/`, `route/`, `api/`, `handler/` | api | 3 |
   123→| `src/core/`, `module/`, `service/` (신규 파일) | architecture | 3 |
   124→| `.eslintrc`, `CONTRIBUTING`, `workflow/` | policy | 3 |
   125→| `Dockerfile`, `k8s/`, `terraform/`, `.github/workflows/` | infrastructure | 3 |
   126→| 기타 | general | 1 |
   127→
   128→**커밋 메시지 키워드 기반 분류 (2차 보조):**
   129→
   130→| 키워드 | 카테고리 | 가중치 |
   131→|--------|---------|--------|
   132→| `endpoint`, `api`, `rest`, `graphql`, `route` | api | 2 |
   133→| `architecture`, `module`, `refactor`, `structure` | architecture | 2 |
   134→| `lint`, `rule`, `policy`, `convention`, `standard` | policy | 2 |
   135→| `deploy`, `docker`, `k8s`, `ci`, `cd`, `infra` | infrastructure | 2 |
   136→
   137→```
   138→분류 알고리즘:
   139→1. 각 변경 파일의 경로 패턴을 분석 → 카테고리별 가중치 합산
   140→2. 커밋 메시지 키워드 분석 → 카테고리별 가중치 추가
   141→3. 가중치 합계가 가장 높은 카테고리 선택
   142→4. 최고 가중치가 동일하면 → 사용자에게 카테고리 선택 질문
   143→5. 모든 카테고리 가중치가 0이면 → general로 분류
   144→```
   145→
   146→### Phase 4: Document Discovery
   147→
   148→```
   149→1. 설정된 컬렉션(collection_id)에서 관련 문서 검색:
   150→   → mcp__outline__search_documents 로 변경 내용 관련 키워드 검색
   151→   → 검색 키워드: 변경된 모듈명, 주요 파일명, 커밋 메시지 핵심 키워드
   152→2. 검색 결과 분석:
   153→   a) 관련 문서 발견 → "기존 문서를 업데이트할까요, 새 문서를 만들까요?" 질문
   154→      - 기존 문서 목록 표시 (제목, 마지막 수정일)
   155→      - 사용자가 업데이트할 문서 선택 또는 신규 생성 선택
   156→   b) 관련 문서 미발견 → 신규 문서 생성 진행
   157→3. 기존 문서 업데이트 선택 시:
   158→   → mcp__outline__read_document 로 기존 문서 내용 로드
   159→   → 기존 내용에 변경사항 병합
   160→```
   161→
   162→### Phase 5: Content Generation & Security Filtering
   163→
   164→```
   165→1. 카테고리별 문서 템플릿에 따라 한국어 문서 생성 (아래 "카테고리별 문서 템플릿" 참조)
   166→2. 보안 필터링 (필수):
   167→   a) 다음 패턴을 감지하여 마스킹:
   168→      - password, secret, api_key, token, credential, private_key
   169→      - db_password, connection_string, aws_access_key
   170→      - Bearer 토큰: Bearer [토큰값] → Bearer [MASKED]
   171→      - SSH 키: -----BEGIN ... PRIVATE KEY----- → [SSH_KEY_MASKED]
   172→      - 사설 IP: 10.x.x.x, 172.16-31.x.x, 192.168.x.x → [PRIVATE_IP_MASKED]
   173→      - .outline-context.json의 sensitive_patterns에 정의된 추가 패턴
   174→   b) 마스킹 적용 후 결과 사용자에게 보고:
   175→      → "다음 민감정보가 마스킹되었습니다: [항목 목록]"
   176→      → 마스킹 항목이 없으면 보고 생략
   177→3. 생성된 문서 내용을 사용자에게 미리보기로 표시
   178→4. 사용자 수정 요청이 있으면 반영
   179→```
   180→
   181→### Phase 6: Write to Outline
   182→
   183→```
   184→1. 사용자에게 최종 확인 요청:

   498→```
   499→
   500→---
   501→
   502→## 8. Boundaries
   503→
   504→**Will:**
   505→- `.outline-context.json`으로 컬렉션 설정 자동 관리
   506→- 변경 파일 분석 및 문서 유형 자동 분류
   507→- 기존 문서 검색 및 업데이트/신규 생성 판단
   508→- 카테고리별 템플릿 기반 한국어 문서 생성
   509→- 민감정보 자동 감지 및 마스킹
   510→- 사용자 확인 후 Outline 위키에 문서 작성
   511→
   512→**Will Not:**
   513→- 사용자 확인 없이 문서 생성/수정
   514→- 문서 삭제 (Outline의 DISABLE_DELETE 설정 준수)
   515→- 코드 자동 수정 또는 커밋
   516→- 여러 컬렉션에 동시 문서 배포
   517→- Outline 워크스페이스 설정 변경
   518→

    91→## 3. Behavioral Flow
    92→
    93→### Phase 1: Context Loading
    94→
    95→```
    96→1. 프로젝트 루트에서 `.plane-context.json` 파일 탐색
    97→2. 파일 존재 → JSON 파싱 → project_identifier 추출
    98→   파일 미존재 → 초기 설정 워크플로우 실행 (위 "설정 파일 초기화" 참고)
    99→3. mcp__plane__list_projects 호출 → project_identifier로 project_id 확인
   100→4. mcp__plane__retrieve_project(project_id) 호출 → 프로젝트 유효성 검증
   101→5. 검증 실패 시 → 사용자에게 알림, 재설정 안내
   102→```
   103→
   104→### Phase 2: Issue Discovery
   105→
   106→```
   107→1. `git branch --show-current` → 현재 브랜치명 확인
   108→2. 정규식으로 이슈 식별자 파싱: /{PREFIX}-(\d+)/ (PREFIX = project_identifier)
   109→   예: feature/PROJ-42-add-cart → PROJ-42
   110→3. 식별자 발견 시:
   111→   → mcp__plane__retrieve_work_item_by_identifier(PROJ-42) → 이슈 자동 연결
   112→   → 이슈 제목, 상태, 담당자 표시
   113→4. 식별자 미발견 시:
   114→   → 사용자에게 이슈 지정 방식 질문:
   115→     a) "이슈 번호 직접 입력" → 번호 입력 → retrieve_work_item_by_identifier
   116→     b) "키워드로 검색" → mcp__plane__search_work_items → 결과 목록에서 선택
   117→     c) "새 이슈 생성" → [issue.html](templates/issue.html) 템플릿 로드 → 변수 바인딩 → mcp__plane__create_work_item(description_html=...)
   118→     d) "이슈 없이 진행" → 이슈 미연결 (Phase 5 이력 기록 생략)
   119→```
   120→
   121→### Phase 3: Work Tracking
   122→
   123→```
   124→1. 연결된 이슈의 현재 상태 확인
   125→2. 상태가 "In Progress"가 아니면:
   126→   → 사용자에게 "상태를 In Progress로 변경할까요?" 확인
   127→   → 승인 시 mcp__plane__list_states → In Progress 상태 ID 조회
   128→   → mcp__plane__update_work_item(state=in_progress_id)
   129→3. 작업 유형 자동 분류 (Smart Categorization):
   130→   a) 브랜치 prefix 분석:
   131→      - feature/, feat/ → Feature
   132→      - fix/, bugfix/, hotfix/ → Bug
   133→      - refactor/ → Refactor
   134→      - chore/, docs/ → Maintenance
   135→   b) 커밋 메시지 패턴 (보조):
   136→      - "fix", "resolve", "close" → Bug
   137→      - "add", "implement" → Feature
   138→      - "refactor", "clean" → Refactor
   139→   c) diff 패턴 (보조):
   140→      - 새 파일 추가 비율 높음 → Feature
   141→      - 기존 파일 수정 위주 → Bug/Refactor
   142→4. `git diff --stat`으로 변경 범위 추적 → 변경 파일 수, 추가/삭제 라인 수 기록
   143→```
   144→
   145→### Phase 4: Scope Analysis & Sub-task Suggestion
   146→
   147→```
   148→1. `git diff --name-only`로 변경 파일 목록 수집
   149→2. 파일 경로 기반 모듈 그룹핑:
   150→   - api/, controller/, route/ → API 모듈
   151→   - service/, usecase/, domain/ → Service 모듈
   152→   - component/, page/, view/ → UI 모듈
   153→   - test/, spec/, __tests__/ → Test 모듈
   154→   - config/, infra/, deploy/ → Infrastructure 모듈
   155→   - migration/, schema/ → Database 모듈
   156→3. Adaptive Depth (변경 규모별 분기):
   157→   a) 소규모 (파일 5개 이하, 모듈 1~2개):
   158→      → 서브태스크 제안 없음, Phase 5에서 간단 코멘트
   159→   b) 중규모 (파일 6~15개, 모듈 2~3개):
   160→      → 선택적 제안: "서브태스크로 분할하시겠습니까?"
   161→   c) 대규모 (파일 16개 이상 또는 모듈 4개 이상):
   162→      → 적극적 분할 제안, 모듈별 서브태스크 초안 제시
   163→4. 사용자 승인 후에만 서브태스크 생성:
   164→   → mcp__plane__create_work_item(parent=원본이슈ID) 으로 하위 작업 생성
   165→   → mcp__plane__create_work_item_relation 으로 종속성 설정
   166→```
   167→
   168→### Phase 5: Completion & History Writing
   169→
   170→```
   171→1. 변경 요약 데이터 수집:
   172→   - `git log --oneline` → 커밋 이력
   173→   - `git diff --stat` → 변경 통계 (파일 수, 추가/삭제 라인)
   174→   - `git diff --name-only` → 변경 파일 목록
   175→2. 자연어 변경 요약 생성:
   176→   - 작업 유형 (Feature/Bug/Refactor)
   177→   - 주요 변경 내용 (커밋 메시지 기반)
   178→   - 영향 범위 (모듈별 변경 파일 수)
   179→3. [comment.html](templates/comment.html) 템플릿 로드 → 변수 바인딩:
   180→      - `{{work_type}}` ← Phase 3에서 분류한 작업 유형
   181→      - `{{branch_name}}` ← 현재 브랜치명
   182→      - `{{natural_language_summary}}` ← 커밋 메시지 기반 자연어 요약
   183→      - `{{files_changed}}`, `{{insertions}}`, `{{deletions}}` ← git diff --stat 파싱
   184→      - `{{changed_files}}` ← git diff --name-only 결과
   185→      - `{{commits}}` ← git log --oneline (hash, message 쌍)
   186→   → mcp__plane__create_work_item_comment(comment_html=바인딩된 HTML)
   187→```
   188→
   189→```
   190→4. (선택) mcp__plane__create_work_log 로 작업 시간 기록
   191→5. 사용자 확인 후 상태 변경:
   192→   → mcp__plane__list_states → 완료 상태(Done 등) ID 조회

   225→## 4. Smart Categorization (작업 유형 자동 분류)
   226→
   227→3중 신호를 분석하여 작업 유형을 자동 분류합니다.
   228→
   229→| 신호 | 우선순위 | 소스 | 분류 규칙 |
   230→|------|----------|------|-----------|
   231→| 브랜치 prefix | 1 (최고) | `git branch --show-current` | `feature/`→Feature, `fix/`→Bug, `refactor/`→Refactor |
   232→| 커밋 메시지 | 2 | `git log --oneline` | 키워드 빈도 분석 |
   233→| diff 패턴 | 3 (최저) | `git diff --stat` | 신규 파일 비율, 수정 패턴 |
   234→
   235→**우선순위 규칙:**
   236→- 브랜치 prefix가 명확하면 최우선 적용
   237→- 브랜치 prefix가 모호하면 (예: `dev/`) 커밋 메시지 + diff 패턴으로 결정
   238→- 모든 신호가 모호하면 사용자에게 직접 질문

   267→| 이력 기록 | `mcp__plane__create_work_item_comment` | 변경 요약 HTML 코멘트 작성 |
   268→| 시간 기록 | `mcp__plane__create_work_log` | 작업 시간 기록 |
   269→| 머지 코멘트 | `mcp__plane__create_work_item_comment` | merge-comment.html 기반 머지 완료 코멘트 (Phase 6) |
   270→| 머지 종료 | `mcp__plane__update_work_item` | state → completed, completed_at 설정 (Phase 6) |
   271→| 관계 설정 | `mcp__plane__create_work_item_relation` | 서브태스크 간 종속성 설정 |
   272→| 사이클 연결 | `mcp__plane__add_work_items_to_cycle` | 스프린트/사이클에 이슈 추가 |
   273→| 모듈 연결 | `mcp__plane__add_work_items_to_module` | 모듈에 이슈 추가 |
   274→
   275→### Git 도구 (Bash)
   276→
   277→| 명령어 | 용도 |
   278→|--------|------|
   279→| `git branch --show-current` | 브랜치명에서 이슈 식별자 파싱 |
   280→| `git diff --stat` | 변경 통계 (파일 수, 라인 수) |
   281→| `git diff --name-only` | 변경 파일 목록 (모듈 그룹핑) |
   282→| `git log --oneline` | 커밋 이력 수집 |
   283→
   284→### 파일 도구
   285→
   286→| 도구 | 용도 |
   287→|------|------|
   288→| **Glob** | `.plane-context.json` 파일 탐색 |
   289→| **Read** | `.plane-context.json` 설정 로드 |
   290→| **Write** | `.plane-context.json` 초기 생성 |

   292→---
   293→
   294→## 7. 브랜치명 파싱 규칙
   295→
   296→### 지원 패턴
   297→
   298→```
   299→{prefix}/{IDENTIFIER}-{number}-{description}
   300→{prefix}/{IDENTIFIER}-{number}
   301→{IDENTIFIER}-{number}-{description}
   302→{IDENTIFIER}-{number}
   303→```
   304→
   305→### 파싱 정규식
   306→
   307→```
   308→/([A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-\d+)/
   309→```
   310→
   311→### 예시
   312→
   313→| 브랜치명 | 파싱 결과 |
   314→|----------|-----------|
   315→| `feature/PROJ-42-add-cart` | `PROJ-42` |
   316→| `fix/PROJ-123-login-bug` | `PROJ-123` |
   317→| `PROJ-7-quick-fix` | `PROJ-7` |
   318→| `refactor/cleanup-utils` | 미발견 → 사용자에게 질문 |
   319→
   320→---
   321→
   322→## 8. Examples
   323→
   324→### 예시 1: 브랜치에서 이슈 자동 감지
   325→
   326→```
   327→사용자: "이슈 연결해줘"
   328→
   329→[Phase 1] .plane-context.json 로드 → project_identifier: "SHOP"
   330→[Phase 2] git branch → feature/SHOP-42-add-cart
   331→          → SHOP-42 파싱 → retrieve_work_item_by_identifier("SHOP-42")
   332→          → "장바구니 기능 추가" 이슈 연결됨
   333→
   334→에이전트: SHOP-42 "장바구니 기능 추가" 이슈에 연결했습니다.
   335→         현재 상태: Backlog
   336→         상태를 In Progress로 변경할까요?
   337→```
   338→
   339→### 예시 2: 키워드 검색으로 이슈 연결
   340→
   341→```
   342→사용자: "이슈 추적 시작"
   343→
   344→[Phase 1] .plane-context.json 로드
   345→[Phase 2] git branch → dev/payment-refactor (이슈 번호 없음)
   346→          → 사용자에게 이슈 지정 방식 질문
   347→
   348→사용자: "결제로 검색해줘"
   349→
   350→[Phase 2] search_work_items("결제") → 3건 발견
   351→          1. SHOP-38 "결제 모듈 리팩토링"
   352→          2. SHOP-41 "결제 오류 수정"
   353→          3. SHOP-45 "결제 수단 추가"
   354→
   355→사용자: "1번"
   356→          → SHOP-38 연결
   357→```
   358→
   359→### 예시 3: 작업 완료 시 자동 제안 (하이브리드)
   360→
   361→```
   362→사용자: "다 했어, 커밋할게"
   363→
   364→에이전트: Plane에 작업 이력을 기록할까요? (연결된 이슈: SHOP-42)
   365→
   366→사용자: "응"
   367→
   368→[Phase 5] git log + git diff → 변경 요약 생성
   369→          → create_work_item_comment (HTML 코멘트 작성)
   370→          → 상태를 Done으로 변경할까요?
   371→```
   372→
   373→### 예시 4: 대규모 변경 시 서브태스크 제안
   374→
   375→```
   376→[Phase 4] git diff --name-only → 22개 파일 변경
   377→          모듈 분석:
   378→          - API: 5개 파일 (controller, route)
   379→          - Service: 8개 파일 (usecase, domain)
   380→          - UI: 6개 파일 (component, page)
   381→          - Test: 3개 파일
   382→
   383→에이전트: 4개 모듈에 걸쳐 22개 파일이 변경되었습니다.
   384→         서브태스크로 분할하시겠습니까?
   385→
   386→         제안:
   387→         1. SHOP-42-1: API 엔드포인트 구현 (5개 파일)
   388→         2. SHOP-42-2: 비즈니스 로직 구현 (8개 파일)
   389→         3. SHOP-42-3: UI 컴포넌트 구현 (6개 파일)
   390→         4. SHOP-42-4: 테스트 코드 작성 (3개 파일)
   391→```
   392→
   393→---
   394→
   395→## 9. Boundaries
   396→
   397→**Will:**
   398→- 브랜치명에서 이슈 번호 자동 파싱
   399→- Plane 이슈 연결, 상태 변경, 코멘트 작성
   400→- 변경 범위 분석 및 서브태스크 분할 제안
   401→- 작업 완료 시 자동 이력 기록 제안
   402→- `.plane-context.json` 자동 생성 및 관리
   403→
   404→**Will Not:**
   405→- 사용자 확인 없이 이슈 상태 변경
   406→- 사용자 승인 없이 서브태스크 생성
   407→- Plane 이슈/프로젝트 삭제
   408→- 코드 자동 수정 또는 커밋
   409→- Plane 워크스페이스 설정 변경

    11→# Obsidian Developer Technical Learning Note System

    16→
    17→## 1. Document Type Detection
    18→
    19→Analyzes keywords from user requests to automatically select the appropriate template from 7 categories.

    21→### Detection Priority
    22→
    23→| Priority | Category | Detection Keywords | Template |
    24→|----------|---------|------------|--------|
    25→| 1 | troubleshooting | error, bug, fix, debug, resolve | [troubleshooting](templates/troubleshooting.md) |
    26→| 2 | comparison | vs, compare, difference, alternative, choose | [comparison](templates/comparison.md) |

   207→FROM ""

   209→  AND date(created) >= date(today) - dur(7 days)
   210→SORT created DESC
   211→LIMIT 10

   275→## 10. Workflow
   276→
   277→### New Note Creation Flow
   278→
   279→```
   280→1. Ctrl+N or Templater shortcut (Alt+1~7)
   281→   |
   282→2. Select template (template matching the category)
   283→   |

   305→## 11. Important Notes
   306→
   307→1. **Frontmatter consistency**: All notes must include YAML frontmatter (DataView queries depend on it)

     3→description: Use this skill when reviewing or writing performance-sensitive code. Provides quick reference for common performance anti-patterns and optimization strategies across Kotlin, Python, and TypeScript/JavaScript.
     4→---
     5→
     6→# Performance Review Quick Reference
     7→
     8→This skill provides a condensed checklist for identifying performance anti-patterns during code review or development.
     9→
    10→## When to Activate
    11→
    12→- Reviewing code that handles high throughput or low-latency requirements
    13→- Writing or modifying database queries, batch processing, or API handlers
    14→- Working with large datasets, collections, or serialization
    15→- Changing concurrency, threading, or async patterns
    16→- Noticing potential memory leaks or excessive object allocation
    17→- Optimizing slow endpoints or background jobs
    18→
    19→## Core Principles
    20→
    21→### 1. Measure First
    22→Never optimize without profiling. Use benchmarks to confirm bottlenecks before refactoring.
    23→
    24→### 2. Focus on Hot Paths
    25→Optimize code that runs frequently (request handlers, loops, batch jobs). Cold paths (startup, config loading) rarely matter.
    26→
    27→### 3. Readability vs Performance
    28→Only sacrifice readability when profiling proves measurable impact. Premature optimization causes maintenance burden.
    29→
    30→## Quick Reference by Category
    31→
    32→### 1. Object Creation & Memory
    33→| Anti-Pattern | Fix | Languages |
    34→|-------------|-----|-----------|
    35→| New ObjectMapper per call | Singleton companion object | Kotlin |
    36→| Missing `__slots__` on data classes | Add `__slots__` | Python |
    37→| `new RegExp()` in functions | Module-level constant | TS/JS |
    38→| Closure retaining large objects | Extract needed values only | TS/JS |
    39→
    40→### 2. Loops & Algorithms
    41→| Anti-Pattern | Fix | Languages |
    42→|-------------|-----|-----------|
    43→| DB call inside loop (N+1) | Batch query (`findAllById`) | All |
    44→| String concatenation in loop | `joinToString` / `StringBuilder` | Kotlin |
    45→| List comprehension for sum | Generator expression | Python |
    46→| DOM append in loop | `DocumentFragment` batching | TS/JS |
    47→
    48→### 3. I/O & Network
    49→| Anti-Pattern | Fix | Languages |
    50→|-------------|-----|-----------|
    51→| N+1 lazy loading | `@EntityGraph` / fetch join | Kotlin |
    52→| `@Transactional` wrapping HTTP calls | Narrow transaction scope | Kotlin |
    53→| Sequential HTTP requests | `asyncio.gather` / `Promise.all` | Python/TS |
    54→| Loading entire file into memory | Stream response | TS/JS |
    55→
    56→### 4. Serialization
    57→| Anti-Pattern | Fix | Languages |
    58→|-------------|-----|-----------|
    59→| New ObjectMapper per request | Inject or companion object | Kotlin |
    60→| `json.loads/dumps` (stdlib) | `orjson` (3-10x faster) | Python |
    61→| `JSON.stringify` for comparison | Deep equality (`isEqual`) | TS/JS |
    62→| Reflection-based DTO mapping | MapStruct (compile-time) | Kotlin |
    63→
    64→### 5. Concurrency
    65→| Anti-Pattern | Fix | Languages |
    66→|-------------|-----|-----------|
    67→| `@Synchronized` on entire method | Minimize critical section | Kotlin |
    68→| `runBlocking` on request thread | `suspend fun` | Kotlin |
    69→| `ThreadPoolExecutor` for CPU work | `ProcessPoolExecutor` | Python |
    70→| Heavy computation on main thread | `Worker` threads | TS/JS |
    71→| Unbounded `Promise.all` | `p-limit` concurrency control | TS/JS |
    72→
    73→### 6. Collections
    74→| Anti-Pattern | Fix | Languages |
    75→|-------------|-----|-----------|
    76→| `List.contains()` in loop | Convert to `HashSet` | Kotlin |
    77→| `list.pop(0)` | `collections.deque` | Python |
    78→| `Array` for large numeric data | `TypedArray` | TS/JS |
    79→| `Object` as dynamic map | `Map` for frequent mutations | TS/JS |
    80→
    81→### 7. Caching
    82→| Anti-Pattern | Fix | Languages |
    83→|-------------|-----|-----------|
    84→| DB query for rarely-changing data | Caffeine cache with TTL | Kotlin |
    85→| Repeated expensive computation | `@cached` / `lru_cache` | Python |
    86→| Strong reference cache | `WeakRef`-based cache | TS/JS |
    87→| Recomputing derived data each render | `useMemo` | React/TS |
    88→
    89→### 8. Logging & Exceptions
    90→| Anti-Pattern | Fix | Languages |
    91→|-------------|-----|-----------|
    92→| String concat in disabled log level | Lambda-based `logger.debug { }` | Kotlin |
    93→| f-string in debug log | `%s` lazy formatting | Python |
    94→| Exceptions for expected flow | `Result` pattern | Kotlin |
    95→| `Error` creation for flow control | Return validation result | TS/JS |
    96→
    97→### 9. Elasticsearch / Search
    98→| Anti-Pattern | Fix | Languages |
    99→|-------------|-----|-----------|
   100→| Single-document indexing in loop | Bulk API | All |
   101→| `from/size` deep pagination | `search_after` | All |
   102→| Expensive aggregation every request | Cache with TTL | All |
   103→| Same analyzer for index & search | Separate analyzers | All |
   104→
   105→## Top 5 Most Common Anti-Patterns
   106→
   107→These are the patterns most frequently encountered in production code reviews:
   108→
   109→### 1. N+1 Queries
   110→```kotlin
   111→// BAD
   112→ids.map { userRepository.findById(it) }
   113→// GOOD
   114→userRepository.findAllById(ids)
   115→```
   116→
   117→### 2. ObjectMapper / JSON Serializer Per Call
   118→```kotlin
   119→// BAD
   120→val mapper = ObjectMapper()
   121→// GOOD
   122→companion object { private val mapper = jacksonObjectMapper() }
   123→```
   124→
   125→### 3. Sequential I/O Where Parallel Is Possible
   126→```typescript
   127→// BAD
   128→const a = await fetchA(); const b = await fetchB()
   129→// GOOD
   130→const [a, b] = await Promise.all([fetchA(), fetchB()])
   131→```
   132→
   133→### 4. Wrong Collection Type for Lookups
   134→```python
   135→# BAD: O(n) per check
   136→if item in large_list: ...
   137→# GOOD: O(1) per check
   138→if item in large_set: ...
   139→```
   140→
   141→### 5. Oversized Transaction Scope
   142→```kotlin
   143→// BAD: @Transactional wrapping external HTTP call
   144→// GOOD: Split into DB-only transaction + separate HTTP call
   145→```
   146→
   147→## Severity Guide
   148→
   149→| Severity | When to Flag |
   150→|----------|-------------|
   151→| **Critical** | OOM risk, deadlock, production outage potential |
   152→| **High** | Measurable latency/throughput degradation |
   153→| **Medium** | Suboptimal but functional, improvement opportunity |
   154→| **Low** | Minor optimization, nice-to-have |
   155→
   156→## Integration with Other Tools
   157→
   158→- Use `/perf-review [target]` command for structured analysis with full report
   159→- Use `/analyze --focus performance` for broader architecture-level review
   160→- The `perf-reviewer` agent contains the complete checklist with all code examples
   161→- This skill provides quick reference during regular development
   162→
   163→---
   164→
   165→**Remember**: Performance matters most in hot paths. Always profile before optimizing, and keep code readable unless the benchmark proves otherwise.
   166→

    27→# Post-Merge - 머지 후 자동화 오케스트레이터

    31→MR(Merge Request) 머지 완료 후 후속 작업을 자동화합니다.
    32→Plane 이슈 종료(코멘트 + 상태 변경)와 Outline 문서 업데이트를 하나의 흐름으로 연계 실행합니다.

    34→
    35→---
    36→
    37→## 1. 활성화 규칙

    39→| 트리거 유형 | 조건 | 동작 |
    40→|-------------|------|------|
    41→| **수동** | "머지 완료", "머지됐어", "post merge" 등 명시적 호출 | Phase 1~6 전체 실행 |
    42→| **머지 요청** | "머지해줘" | Phase 1(경로 C)에서 `glab mr merge` 실행 후 Phase 2~6 진행 |
    43→| **Hook 연동** | `glab mr merge` 성공 감지 (PostToolUse Hook) | "머지 후 Plane/Outline 처리를 진행할까요?" 제안 → 승인 시 Phase 1~6 실행 |
    44→| **자동 제안** | "머지", "merge" 키워드 감지 | "머지 후 Plane/Outline 처리를 진행할까요?" 질문 → 승인 시 실행 |
    45→
    46→---
    47→
    48→## 2. Behavioral Flow
    49→
    50→### Phase 1: 머지 감지 & MR 컨텍스트 수집
    51→
    52→```
    53→1. MR 정보 확보 (경로 분기):
    54→   경로 A: Hook에서 호출됨 → MR ID가 이미 전달됨
    55→   경로 B: "머지됐어" / "머지 완료"
    56→     → git branch --show-current → 현재 브랜치명 확인
    57→     → glab mr list --source-branch={branch} --state merged -F json
    58→     → 최근 머지된 MR 선택
    59→   경로 C: "머지해줘"
    60→     → glab mr list --source-branch={branch} --state opened -F json
    61→     → 열린 MR 확인 → glab mr merge {id} 실행
    62→     → 머지 완료 후 계속
    63→
    64→2. MR 상세 정보 수집:
    65→   → glab mr view {id} -F json
    66→   → 추출: MR 제목, 설명, 소스 브랜치, 타겟 브랜치, 변경 파일 수, 라벨
    67→
    68→3. Plane 이슈 ID 파싱:
    69→   → 소스 브랜치명에서 정규식 /([A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-\d+)/ 로 이슈 식별자 추출
    70→   → 예: feature/PROJ-42-add-cart → PROJ-42
    71→   → 미발견 시 사용자에게 이슈 번호 질문 (선택적)
    72→```
    73→
    74→### Phase 2: Plane 이슈 종료 (issue-tracker Phase 6 위임)
    75→
    76→```
    77→1. .plane-context.json 로드 → project_identifier, project_id 확인
    78→   → 파일 미존재 시 사용자에게 안내 후 Phase 3으로 건너뜀

    80→2. mcp__plane__retrieve_work_item_by_identifier({이슈 식별자})

    85→   → 변수 바인딩:

    88→     - {{merge_date}} ← 오늘 날짜 (YYYY-MM-DD)

    97→
    98→4. 이슈 상태 변경:
    99→   → mcp__plane__list_states(project_id)
   100→   → group이 "completed"인 상태 ID 조회
   101→   → mcp__plane__update_work_item(

   104→     )
   105→   → 완료 알림: "PROJ-42 이슈가 종료되었습니다"
   106→```
   107→
   108→### Phase 3: 문서화 필요성 판단
   109→
   110→```

   125→```
   126→
   127→### Phase 4: Outline 문서 업데이트 (document-lastest Phase 2~6 위임)
   128→
   129→```

   138→   → Phase 3: Document Type Detection

   141→   → Phase 6: Write to Outline
   142→
   143→3. 문서 URL 수집 → Phase 2의 merge-comment에 역바인딩

   161→```

   165→```
   166→1. "로컬 브랜치를 삭제할까요?" 질문

    26→---
    27→
    28→# Sync CLAUDE.md - Automatic CLAUDE.md Synchronization Based on Code Changes
    29→
    30→## Overview
    31→
    32→Automatically analyzes whether work should be reflected in CLAUDE.md before commit/push or PR/MR, and performs updates when necessary.
    33→If the `monorepo-init` skill is responsible for **creating** CLAUDE.md, this skill is responsible for **maintaining** CLAUDE.md after work is completed.
    34→
    35→---
    36→
    37→## 1. Activation Rules
    38→
    39→| Trigger Type | Condition | Behavior |
    40→|-------------|-----------|----------|
    41→| **Manual** | Explicit invocation such as "CLAUDE.md sync", "sync claude md" | Execute full Phase 1~5 |
    42→| **Auto-suggest** | Completion signal detected such as "commit", "push", "create PR" | Ask "Shall I check whether CLAUDE.md needs to be updated?" → Execute upon approval |
    43→
    44→---
    45→
    46→## 2. Behavioral Flow
    47→
    48→### Phase 1: CLAUDE.md Discovery and Loading
    49→
    50→```
    51→1. Search for CLAUDE.md location from the project root (Glob: **/CLAUDE.md)
    52→   - Priority: CLAUDE.md > claude/CLAUDE.md > .claude/CLAUDE.md
    53→2. If CLAUDE.md does not exist:
    54→   → Output "CLAUDE.md does not exist. Please run monorepo-init or project initialization first." and stop
    55→3. Read current CLAUDE.md content and identify existing section list
    56→4. Check if CLAUDE.md already has staged changes:
    57→   → git diff --cached -- "**/CLAUDE.md"
    58→   → Notify user if changes are already staged
    59→```
    60→
    61→### Phase 2: Collecting Change Scope
    62→
    63→Auto-detect mode:
    64→
    65→| Condition | Analysis Target | Description |
    66→|-----------|----------------|-------------|
    67→| Staged changes exist | `git diff --cached` | Pre-commit scenario |
    68→| User mentions "PR", "MR" | `git diff main...HEAD` | Pre-PR scenario |
    69→| Fallback | `git diff HEAD` | All uncommitted changes |
    70→
    71→Collected items:
    72→```
    73→1. git diff --name-only → List of changed files
    74→2. git diff --stat → Change statistics (number of files, added/deleted lines)
    75→3. git diff → Actual diff content (for change classification)
    76→```
    77→
    78→### Phase 3: Change Classification (Determining Update Necessity)
    79→
    80→Analyzes the collected diff to determine whether CLAUDE.md update is necessary.
    81→
    82→**Update Required (Yes):**
    83→
    84→| Change Category | Detection Signals |
    85→|---|---|
    86→| Architecture change | New directory structure created, module boundary changes, layer additions |
    87→| New integration/MCP | `mcp/` file changes, new external service clients, API integration additions |
    88→| Convention/pattern change | Linter config changes, new coding standard files, new common utility/base classes |
    89→| Environment/tool change | Dockerfile, docker-compose, CI/CD config, Makefile changes |
    90→| Major dependency addition | New framework/library additions (excluding patch updates) |
    91→| Workflow change | New git hooks, new scripts, new CI stages |
    92→| Skill/command addition | New files in `skills/`, `commands/`, `claude/commands/` |
    93→
    94→**No Update Required (No):**
    95→
    96→| Change Category | Description |
    97→|---|---|
    98→| Simple bug fix | Minor changes to existing files, no new patterns |
    99→| Feature addition within existing patterns | New feature files following existing structure |
   100→| Test addition | Test files following existing test conventions |
   101→| Documentation changes | README, docs, comment changes |
   102→| Refactoring | Renames, moves within existing patterns |
   103→
   104→**Detection Pattern Details:**
   105→
   106→```
   107→# Architecture change detection
   108→- Were new directories created? (new path patterns in diff)
   109→- Were new submodules added to core directories such as src/, lib/, packages/?
   110→
   111→# New integration/MCP detection
   112→- Were mcp/*.json files added/modified?
   113→- Were new API client files added?
   114→
   115→# Convention change detection
   116→- Config file changes such as .eslintrc, .prettierrc, tsconfig.json, pyproject.toml
   117→- New common pattern files such as base classes, mixins, decorators added
   118→
   119→# Environment/tool change detection
   120→- Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml added/modified
   121→- .github/workflows/, .gitlab-ci.yml, Jenkinsfile changes
   122→- Makefile, justfile, taskfile.yml changes
   123→
   124→# Major dependency detection
   125→- New dependency additions in package.json, requirements.txt, go.mod, build.gradle, etc.
   126→  (Excluding version bumps only)
   127→
   128→# Skill/command detection
   129→- New skills/*/SKILL.md files
   130→- New claude/commands/*.md files
   131→- Config changes within .claude/ directory
   132→```
   133→
   134→### Phase 4: Decision and Proposal
   135→
   136→**When no update is required:**
   137→
   138→```
   139→No CLAUDE.md update is needed.
   140→
   141→Analysis results:
   142→- Change type: {bug fix / feature addition within existing patterns / test addition / ...}
   143→- Changed files: {N}
   144→- Impact scope: Within existing architecture/rules
   145→```
   146→→ Stop here
   147→
   148→**When update is required:**
   149→
   150→```
   151→1. Identify which sections need to be added/modified
   152→   - Match against existing CLAUDE.md section structure
   153→   - Determine whether a new section is needed or updating an existing section is sufficient
   154→
   155→2. Propose draft update content:
   156→   - Provide rationale linked to changed files
   157→   - Preview specific content to be added/modified
   158→
   159→3. Share "Proceeding with CLAUDE.md update" with user
   160→   → Proceed to Phase 5 without waiting for user response
   161→```
   162→
   163→### Phase 5: Execute CLAUDE.md Update
   164→
   165→```
   166→1. Read current CLAUDE.md content (Read)
   167→2. Apply changes:
   168→   - Update existing sections: Modify section content (Edit)
   169→   - Add new sections: Insert at appropriate location (Edit)
   170→   - Remove obsolete content: Delete information that is no longer valid
   171→3. Write CLAUDE.md file (Write/Edit)
   172→4. Provide agents-md-copy skill integration guidance:
   173→   → "To also update AGENTS.md, run the agents-md-copy skill."
   174→5. Display change diff summary:
   175→   → Summarize added, modified, and deleted content
   176→6. Suggest git add:
   177→   → "Stage the changes with git add {CLAUDE.md path}."
   178→```
   179→
   180→---
   181→
   182→## 3. Update Section Mapping
   183→
   184→Provides guidance on which sections of CLAUDE.md should be updated for each change category.
   185→
   186→| Change Category | Target CLAUDE.md Section | Update Content |
   187→|---|---|---|
   188→| Architecture change | Architecture / Structure | Reflect new modules, directory structure |
   189→| New integration/MCP | Integrations / MCP | Add new MCP servers, external integrations |
   190→| Convention/pattern change | Conventions / Coding Standards | Document new rules, patterns |
   191→| Environment/tool change | Development Setup / Commands | Add new tools, commands |
   192→| Major dependency addition | Tech Stack / Dependencies | Record new libraries |
   193→| Workflow change | Workflow / CI/CD | Document new workflow stages |
   194→| Skill/command addition | Skills / Commands | Update skill, command listings |
   195→
   196→---
   197→
   198→## 4. Tool Coordination
   199→
   200→| Tool | Purpose |
   201→|------|---------|
   202→| **Glob** | Search for `**/CLAUDE.md` file locations |
   203→| **Read** | Read current CLAUDE.md content, analyze config files |
   204→| **Bash** | Collect change scope with `git diff`, `git diff --cached`, `git diff main...HEAD`, etc. |
   205→| **Grep** | Detect patterns in diff content (new imports, config files, MCP configs, etc.) |
   206→| **Edit** | Modify existing CLAUDE.md sections |
   207→| **Write** | Add new sections to CLAUDE.md (when needed) |
   208→
   209→---
   210→
   211→## 5. Examples
   212→
   213→### Example 1: Sync after adding an MCP server
   214→
   215→```
   216→User: "Sync CLAUDE.md"
   217→
   218→[Phase 1] CLAUDE.md discovery → ./CLAUDE.md found, content loaded
   219→[Phase 2] git diff --cached → mcp/grafana.json added
   220→[Phase 3] Classification: New integration/MCP → Update required
   221→[Phase 4] Proposal:
   222→  - Add Grafana MCP server to "Integrations" or "MCP" section
   223→  - Rationale: mcp/grafana.json new file
   224→
   225→Agent: Adding Grafana MCP integration info to CLAUDE.md.
   226→[Phase 5] Execute CLAUDE.md update → Display diff summary
   227→```
   228→
   229→### Example 2: Sync after adding a new skill
   230→
   231→```
   232→User: "I'm going to commit"
   233→Agent: Shall I check whether CLAUDE.md needs to be updated?
   234→User: "Yes"
   235→
   236→[Phase 1] CLAUDE.md discovery → ./CLAUDE.md found
   237→[Phase 2] git diff --cached → skills/sync-claude-md/SKILL.md added
   238→[Phase 3] Classification: Skill/command addition → Update required
   239→[Phase 4] Proposal:
   240→  - Add sync-claude-md skill to "Skills" section
   241→  - Rationale: skills/sync-claude-md/SKILL.md new file
   242→
   243→Agent: Adding sync-claude-md skill info to CLAUDE.md.
   244→[Phase 5] Execute CLAUDE.md update → Display diff summary
   245→         → Sync AGENTS.md as well using the agents-md-copy skill.
   246→```
   247→
   248→### Example 3: Simple bug fix (no update required)
   249→
   250→```
   251→User: "Sync CLAUDE.md"
   252→
   253→[Phase 1] CLAUDE.md discovery → ./CLAUDE.md found
   254→[Phase 2] git diff HEAD → src/utils/format.ts 1 file, 3 lines modified
   255→[Phase 3] Classification: Simple bug fix → No update required
   256→
   257→Agent:
   258→No CLAUDE.md update is needed.
   259→
   260→Analysis results:
   261→- Change type: Bug fix
   262→- Changed files: 1
   263→- Impact scope: Within existing architecture/rules
   264→```
   265→
   266→### Example 4: Full change analysis before PR
   267→
   268→```
   269→User: "Check CLAUDE.md before creating the PR"

   271→[Phase 1] CLAUDE.md discovery → ./CLAUDE.md found

   273→          → 12 files changed, docker-compose.yml added, .github/workflows/ci.yml modified
   274→[Phase 3] Classification:
   275→  - Environment/tool change (docker-compose.yml) → Update required

     4→---
     5→
     6→# Test-Driven Development Workflow
     7→
     8→This skill ensures all code development follows TDD principles with comprehensive test coverage.
     9→
    10→## When to Activate
    11→
    12→- Writing new features or functionality
    13→- Fixing bugs or issues
    14→- Refactoring existing code
    15→- Adding API endpoints
    16→- Creating new components
    17→
    18→## Core Principles
    19→
    20→### 1. Tests BEFORE Code
    21→ALWAYS write tests first, then implement code to make tests pass.
    22→
    23→### 2. Coverage Requirements
    24→- Minimum 80% coverage (unit + integration + E2E)
    25→- All edge cases covered
    26→- Error scenarios tested
    27→- Boundary conditions verified
    28→
    29→### 3. Test Types
    30→
    31→#### Unit Tests
    32→- Individual functions and utilities
    33→- Component logic
    34→- Pure functions
    35→- Helpers and utilities
    36→
    37→#### Integration Tests
    38→- API endpoints
    39→- Database operations
    40→- Service interactions
    41→- External API calls
    42→
    43→#### E2E Tests (Playwright)
    44→- Critical user flows
    45→- Complete workflows
    46→- Browser automation
    47→- UI interactions
    48→
    49→#### Kotlin-Specific Test Types
    50→
    51→| Test Style | Framework | Use Case |
    52→|-----------|-----------|----------|
    53→| `BehaviorSpec` | Kotest | Given/When/Then BDD-style tests |
    54→| `FunSpec` | Kotest | Simple function-level unit tests |
    55→| `StringSpec` | Kotest | One-liner concise tests |
    56→| `@WebMvcTest` | Spring Boot Test | Controller layer tests (MockMvc) |
    57→| `@SpringBootTest` | Spring Boot Test | Full integration tests (TestRestTemplate) |
    58→| `@DataJpaTest` | Spring Boot Test | Repository/JPA layer tests |
    59→
    60→## TDD Workflow Steps
    61→
    62→### Step 1: Write User Journeys
    63→```
    64→As a [role], I want to [action], so that [benefit]
    65→
    66→Example:
    67→As a user, I want to search for markets semantically,
    68→so that I can find relevant markets even without exact keywords.
    69→```
    70→
    71→### Step 2: Generate Test Cases
    72→For each user journey, create comprehensive test cases:
    73→
    74→```typescript
    75→describe('Semantic Search', () => {
    76→  it('returns relevant markets for query', async () => {
    77→    // Test implementation
    78→  })
    79→
    80→  it('handles empty query gracefully', async () => {
    81→    // Test edge case
    82→  })
    83→
    84→  it('falls back to substring search when Redis unavailable', async () => {
    85→    // Test fallback behavior
    86→  })
    87→
    88→  it('sorts results by similarity score', async () => {
    89→    // Test sorting logic
    90→  })
    91→})
    92→```
    93→
    94→### Step 3: Run Tests (They Should Fail)
    95→```bash
    96→npm test
    97→# Tests should fail - we haven't implemented yet
    98→```
    99→
   100→### Step 4: Implement Code
   101→Write minimal code to make tests pass:
   102→
   103→```typescript
   104→// Implementation guided by tests
   105→export async function searchMarkets(query: string) {
   106→  // Implementation here
   107→}
   108→```
   109→
   110→### Step 5: Run Tests Again
   111→```bash
   112→npm test
   113→# Tests should now pass
   114→```
   115→
   116→### Step 6: Refactor
   117→Improve code quality while keeping tests green:
   118→- Remove duplication
   119→- Improve naming
   120→- Optimize performance

   769→    jacoco

   772→jacoco {

   782→}

   794→            limit {

   798→        }
   799→    }
   800→}

   802→
   803→#### Kotlin Test Dependencies (build.gradle.kts)
   804→```kotlin
   805→dependencies {
   806→    // Kotest
   807→    testImplementation("io.kotest:kotest-runner-junit5:5.8.0")
   808→    testImplementation("io.kotest:kotest-assertions-core:5.8.0")
   809→    testImplementation("io.kotest.extensions:kotest-extensions-spring:1.1.3")
   810→    // MockK
   811→    testImplementation("io.mockk:mockk:1.13.9")
   812→    testImplementation("com.ninja-squad:springmockk:4.0.2")
   813→    // Spring Boot Test (exclude Mockito)

   824→
   825→### Kotlin Testing Mistakes to Avoid
   826→
   827→#### ❌ WRONG: Using Mockito Instead of MockK
   828→```kotlin
   829→// Mockito is Java-centric, doesn't support Kotlin features well
   830→@Mock lateinit var service: LiquidityService // Breaks with final classes
   831→```
   832→
   833→#### ✅ CORRECT: Use MockK for Kotlin

   836→val service = mockk<LiquidityService>()
   837→```
   838→
   839→#### ❌ WRONG: @SpringBootTest for Every Test
   840→```kotlin

   843→class SimpleUtilTest { /* ... */ }
   844→```
   845→
   846→#### ✅ CORRECT: Use Appropriate Test Slice
   847→```kotlin

   849→class SimpleUtilTest : FunSpec({ /* ... */ })
   850→
   851→// Controller only - use @WebMvcTest
   852→@WebMvcTest(MarketController::class)

   854→
   855→// Repository only - use @DataJpaTest
   856→@DataJpaTest

   858→```
   859→
   860→#### ❌ WRONG: Not Cleaning Up MockK State
   861→```kotlin

   863→every { service.calculate(any()) } returns 95.0
   864→```
   865→
   866→#### ✅ CORRECT: Use clearAllMocks or confirmVerified
   867→```kotlin
   868→afterEach {
   869→    clearAllMocks()
   870→}
   871→```
   872→
   873→## Common Testing Mistakes to Avoid
   874→
   875→### ❌ WRONG: Testing Implementation Details
   876→```typescript
   877→// Don't test internal state
   878→expect(component.state.count).toBe(5)
   879→```
   880→
   881→### ✅ CORRECT: Test User-Visible Behavior
   882→```typescript
   883→// Test what users see
   884→expect(screen.getByText('Count: 5')).toBeInTheDocument()
   885→```
   886→
   887→### ❌ WRONG: Brittle Selectors
   888→```typescript
   889→// Breaks easily
   890→await page.click('.css-class-xyz')
   891→```
   892→
   893→### ✅ CORRECT: Semantic Selectors
   894→```typescript
   895→// Resilient to changes
   896→await page.click('button:has-text("Submit")')
   897→await page.click('[data-testid="submit-button"]')
   898→```
   899→
   900→### ❌ WRONG: No Test Isolation
   901→```typescript
   902→// Tests depend on each other
   903→test('creates user', () => { /* ... */ })
   904→test('updates same user', () => { /* depends on previous test */ })
   905→```
   906→
   907→### ✅ CORRECT: Independent Tests
   908→```typescript
   909→// Each test sets up its own data
   910→test('creates user', () => {
   911→  const user = createTestUser()
   912→  // Test logic
   913→})
   914→
   915→test('updates user', () => {
   916→  const user = createTestUser()
   917→  // Update logic
   918→})
   919→```
   920→
   921→## Continuous Testing
   922→
   923→### Watch Mode During Development
   924→```bash

   927→```
   928→
   929→### Pre-Commit Hook

   934→
   935→### CI/CD Integration

   943→
   944→### Kotlin Continuous Testing
   945→
   946→```bash

   948→./gradlew test --continuous
   949→

   951→./gradlew test --tests "com.example.service.LiquidityServiceTest"
   952→
   953→# Run tests matching pattern
   954→./gradlew test --tests "*Liquidity*"
   955→
   956→# Lint check before commit
   957→./gradlew ktlintCheck test
   958→```
   959→
   960→#### Kotlin CI/CD Integration (GitHub Actions)
   961→```yaml
   962→# .github/workflows/test-kotlin.yml
   963→name: Kotlin Tests
   964→on: [push, pull_request]
   965→

   987→## Best Practices
   988→
   989→1. **Write Tests First** - Always TDD
   990→2. **One Assert Per Test** - Focus on single behavior
   991→3. **Descriptive Test Names** - Explain what's tested
   992→4. **Arrange-Act-Assert** - Clear test structure
   993→5. **Mock External Dependencies** - Isolate unit tests
   994→6. **Test Edge Cases** - Null, undefined, empty, large
   995→7. **Test Error Paths** - Not just happy paths
